ferry crossing = a journey by boat that carries people and often cars across water
shuttle bus = a bus that runs back and forth between two points, such as a hotel and an airport
park and ride = a car park outside a city with a bus into the centre
high-speed rail = trains that travel much faster than ordinary services
sleeper train = a night train with beds so you travel while you sleep
buffet car = the carriage on a train where you can buy drinks and snacks
hitchhiking = travelling by asking drivers to take you for free
car sharing = several people travelling in one car to cut cost and traffic
express coach = a long-distance bus that makes few stops
cycle path = a route for bicycles, often separated from cars
B&B = a small guesthouse that includes breakfast in the price
self-catering = accommodation with a kitchen so you cook your own meals
overbooking = accepting more reservations than there are rooms or seats
half board = a hotel deal that includes breakfast and one other meal
full board = a hotel deal that includes breakfast, lunch and dinner
en suite = a bedroom with its own private bathroom attached
boutique hotel = a small, stylish hotel, often with an individual design
holiday let = a flat or house rented to tourists for a short stay
timeshare = a scheme where you buy the right to use a holiday property for a set week each year
glamping = camping with extra comfort, such as a proper bed or a cabin
